name: Pad Thai
description: Stir-fried rice noodles with egg, tamarind, fish sauce, sugar, bean sprouts and usually shrimp, topped with crushed peanuts and lime. It is Thailand's best-known noodle dish abroad and a staple of Bangkok street stalls.
how_to_eat: Squeeze over the lime and add chilli flakes, sugar or fish sauce from the table caddy to taste.
how_to_order: Ask for 'phat thai kung' (with shrimp) at street woks and night markets.

name: Tom Yum Goong
description: A hot and sour soup of lemongrass, galangal, kaffir lime leaves, chillies and lime juice, usually made with prawns. It is one of the signature dishes of Central Thai cooking.
how_to_eat: Eat with steamed jasmine rice; the herbs are for flavour and are usually left aside.
how_to_order: Ask for 'tom yam kung', either 'nam sai' (clear) or 'nam khon' (creamy).

name: Green Curry
local_name: แกงเขียวหวาน
description: Kaeng khiao wan is a coconut-milk curry made with green chilli paste and Thai basil, usually with chicken, beef or fish balls. It is a classic Central Thai curry.
how_to_eat: Spoon over steamed jasmine rice or eat with khanom chin rice noodles.
how_to_order: Ask for 'kaeng khiao wan kai' (chicken) at curry-and-rice shops.

name: Pad Kaphrao
description: Minced or sliced meat or seafood stir-fried with holy basil, garlic and bird's eye chilli, seasoned with fish sauce and soy sauce. It is one of Thailand's most common one-plate meals.
how_to_eat: Eat over rice, ideally with a crispy fried egg on top.
how_to_order: Ask for 'khao phat kaphrao mu' (pork) and add 'khai dao' for a fried egg.

name: Khao Man Kai
local_name: ข้าวมันไก่
description: Thai version of Hainanese chicken rice: poached chicken served on rice cooked in chicken fat and garlic, with a cup of broth and a ginger, chilli and fermented soybean sauce.
how_to_eat: Pour the sauce over the chicken and sip the broth between bites.
how_to_order: Look for stalls with whole poached chickens hanging in the window.

name: Boat Noodles
local_name: ก๋วยเตี๋ยวเรือ
description: Kuai tiao ruea are rice noodles with pork or beef in a dark, rich broth spiced with cinnamon and star anise, often thickened with blood. Once sold from boats on the canals, they come in small bowls.
how_to_eat: Order several small bowls and season with chilli, vinegar and sugar.
how_to_order: Ask for 'kuai tiao ruea' with 'mu' (pork) or 'nuea' (beef).

name: Mango Sticky Rice
local_name: ข้าวเหนียวมะม่วง
description: Khao niao mamuang is sticky rice soaked in sweetened, salted coconut milk and served with ripe yellow mango, sometimes topped with roasted mung beans or sesame. It is a popular street dessert, best in the April-May mango season.
how_to_eat: Eat the mango and rice together, with extra coconut cream poured over.
how_to_order: Ask for 'khao niao mamuang' at dessert stalls and markets.

name: Thai Iced Tea
description: Cha yen is strong black tea brewed with spices, sweetened with sugar and condensed milk and served over ice, topped with evaporated or whole milk. It is sold everywhere in bright orange cups.
how_to_order: Ask for 'cha yen' at drink stalls; 'cha dam yen' is the version without milk.

name: Khao Soi
description: A curried coconut noodle soup with boiled egg noodles, topped with crispy fried noodles, usually with chicken or beef. It is the signature dish of Chiang Mai, shared with Laos and Myanmar.
how_to_eat: Add the pickled mustard greens, shallots and lime served on the side.
how_to_order: Ask for 'khao soi kai' (chicken) at noodle shops in Chiang Mai.

name: Khanom Chin Nam Ngiao
local_name: ขนมจีนน้ำเงี้ยว
description: Fermented rice noodles in a tomato and pork broth with pork blood tofu, flavoured with dried red cotton tree flowers. It is a classic Northern Thai noodle dish.
how_to_eat: Eat with the fresh herbs, beansprouts and cabbage served alongside.
how_to_order: Ask for 'khanom chin nam ngiao' at northern noodle stalls.

name: Sai Ua
description: A grilled sausage of fatty minced pork mixed with lemongrass, galangal, kaffir lime leaves, chillies and garlic. It is a hallmark of Northern Thai and Lao cooking.
how_to_eat: Eat in slices with sticky rice and fresh vegetables.
how_to_order: Buy by the coil or slice at northern markets.

name: Nam Phrik Num
local_name: น้ำพริกหนุ่ม
description: A chunky dip of roasted young green chillies, shallots and garlic pounded together. It is a staple Northern Thai relish.
how_to_eat: Scoop with sticky rice, boiled vegetables or pork crackling (khaep mu).
how_to_order: Buy in bags at northern markets, often sold with pork crackling.

name: Kaeng Hang Le
description: A Burmese-influenced stewed pork curry with peanuts, tamarind and dried chillies, made without coconut milk. It is a festive Northern Thai curry.
how_to_eat: Eat with sticky rice or steamed rice.
how_to_order: Ask for 'kaeng hang le' at northern curry shops.

name: Kaeng Khanun
description: A Northern Thai curry of young jackfruit cooked with pork and tomatoes.
how_to_eat: Eat with sticky rice.
how_to_order: Look for it at northern rice-and-curry stalls.

name: Som Tam
description: Green papaya salad pounded in a mortar with chillies, lime, fish sauce, palm sugar, tomatoes and dried shrimp; the Central version adds peanuts, while Isan versions use fermented fish. It is the most famous dish of the Northeast.
how_to_eat: Eat with sticky rice and grilled chicken.
how_to_order: Ask for 'som tam Thai' (milder, with peanuts) or 'som tam pu pla ra' (Isan style) and say how many chillies.

name: Larb
description: A spicy, sour salad of minced meat with lime, fish sauce, chillies, herbs and toasted ground rice. It is a signature dish of Isan and Laos.
how_to_eat: Eat with sticky rice and raw vegetables.
how_to_order: Ask for 'lap mu' (pork) or 'lap kai' (chicken) at Isan restaurants.

name: Kai Yang
description: Marinated grilled chicken shared by Lao and Thai cooking. It is a pillar of Isan street food.
how_to_eat: Dip in jaew chilli sauce and eat with som tam and sticky rice.
how_to_order: Buy by the half or whole bird from charcoal grills.

name: Nam Tok
description: A spicy salad of sliced grilled pork or beef with lime, fish sauce, chillies, herbs and toasted rice powder. The name means 'waterfall', after the juices dripping from the grilling meat.
how_to_eat: Eat with sticky rice.
how_to_order: Ask for 'mu nam tok' (pork) or 'nuea nam tok' (beef).

name: Sai Krok Isan
local_name: ไส้กรอกอีสาน
description: A sour fermented sausage of fatty pork and sticky rice with garlic, left to ferment for a few days before grilling. It originated in Isan.
how_to_eat: Eat with bird's eye chillies, raw cabbage and sliced ginger.
how_to_order: Buy grilled on skewers at markets and street grills.

name: Sticky Rice
local_name: ข้าวเหนียว
description: Glutinous rice steamed in bamboo baskets, the daily staple of northern and northeastern Thailand. It is served with almost every Isan meal.
how_to_eat: Roll a small ball with your fingers and use it to scoop up food.
how_to_order: Ask for 'khao niao'; it comes in small woven baskets.

name: Kaeng Tai Pla
description: A thick, very spicy turmeric curry made with tai pla, a pungent sauce of fermented fish innards, plus shrimp paste and vegetables. It is one of the most typical Southern Thai dishes.
how_to_eat: Eat with rice and plenty of fresh vegetables.
how_to_order: Ask for 'kaeng tai pla' at southern curry-and-rice shops.

name: Kaeng Lueang
description: The southern form of sour curry: a turmeric-yellow, sour and fiery curry without coconut milk, usually with fish and vegetables.
how_to_eat: Eat with steamed rice.
how_to_order: Ask for 'kaeng lueang pla' (with fish).

name: Khua Kling
description: A very spicy dry-fried curry of minced meat with curry paste and shredded kaffir lime leaves. It is a Southern Thai classic.
how_to_eat: Eat with rice and raw vegetables to cool the heat.
how_to_order: Ask for 'khua kling mu' (pork) or 'khua kling nuea' (beef).

name: Khao Yam
description: A Southern Thai rice salad of rice with toppings such as toasted coconut, herbs, dried shrimp and a fermented fish sauce called budu, served unmixed.
how_to_eat: Pour over the sauce and mix everything together before eating.
how_to_order: Ask for 'khao yam' at southern breakfast stalls and markets.

name: Massaman Curry
local_name: แกงมัสมั่น
description: A rich, mild coconut curry with roasted dry spices, potatoes and peanuts, usually with beef or chicken. It comes from Thailand's Muslim cooking tradition.
how_to_eat: Eat with rice or roti.
how_to_order: Ask for 'kaeng matsaman' with 'kai' (chicken) or 'nuea' (beef).
